They're somewhat different technologies. Replicators can only ploduce comparatively simple matter. The transporter buffer can dematerialize and rematerialize complex matter, but generally only through a continuous analogue process. Imagine the two processes like a 3d printer on the one hand, and on the other hand disassembling, shipping, and reassembling a car in another location. Someone who doesn't understand the limitations of the 3d printer might suggest that we just scan and print all the parts, which in theory could work if we had a sufficiently advanced 3d printer, but we don't have 3d printers that are that advanced. They're just different technologies with different limitations to each.
